newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercial demand, CBOT soy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercial demand, CBOT soy.

text.p: WCE canola ended up on ADM and Cargill demand as the CBOT soycomplex closed up, traders said.

"ADM bought 700 July-Nov at $31, Cargill was a noted buyer. The weekly canola crush number was big, it was supportive," a trader said. Crushers used up 54,783 tonnes of canola in the week ended May 14, near the top end of weekly usage. July WCE futures crush margin fell to -4.06 Friday from -2.77 Thursday. About 700 July-Nov spread at $31, May-July $4. Volume was 4,530 lots, or 90,600 tonnes.
July canola rose $3.50 to $418.10, November up $2.50 to $387. July flax rose $0.20 to $333, November up $1.10 to $321.
UGG sold flax to commercials. About 200 May-July spread at $0.50. Russia was rumoured to have bought 5,000 tonnes of linoil, traders said. Volume was 800 lots.
July feed wheat fell $0.10 to $158.60 on hedge selling. July-Dec spread at $2. Volume was 382 lots.
May western barley up $1.60 to $138.60 as RBC-DS bought from Alberta Wheat Pool, July up $0.80 to $137 on commercial demand, traders said. Volume was 500 lots.
UGG sold July oats down US$2 at $116.50 to RBC-DS, a trader said. Volume was 95 lots. RBC-DS sold October feed peas unchanged at US$191.50 to PCTS, traders said. Volume was 50.
The WCE will be closed Monday for Victoria Day holiday.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
